screening_decisions.reason: RCT of HF patients aged 75\u00b18. Intervention: tablet computer with software providing HF information/lifestyle advice (mHealth education). Comparator: standard HF information (usual care). Meets all criteria.
RCT of stable HF patients. Intervention: web-based education via heartfailurematters.org (mHealth) + e-health pathway. Comparator: usual care. Meets all criteria.
RCT pilot with HF patients; web-based self-care intervention (mHealth education) vs implied usual care. Meets criteria; small sample but design is RCT.
RCT of HF patients. Intervention includes SMS follow-up (mHealth-delivered education/reminders). Comparator: regular follow-up (usual care). SMS arm meets mHealth education criterion.

RCT of HF patient-caregiver dyads. Intervention includes computer-based education (mHealth) alongside face-to-face counseling. Mixed delivery, but contains a clear mHealth component vs usual care. Conservative inclusion.
Companion cost-effectiveness analysis of the same RCT as Study 5; same inclusion rationale. Includes computer-based education as part of intervention.

RCT of HF patients, but intervention is nurse-guided education + telephone communication, not clearly mHealth (telephone not listed as mHealth education mode per criteria). Not an app/web/SMS education program.
RCT of HF patients; video education as adjunct to standard education. Delivery mode not specified as mHealth (no mention of smartphone/tablet/web). Likely non-mobile video.
Pilot usability study with 8 patients; no randomization, no comparison group. Not an RCT.
Recruitment process analysis, not an RCT; no comparison of intervention outcomes. Not a primary trial.
RCT of HF patients, but intervention is a compliance monitoring device, not an educational program. Focus is on monitoring adherence, not delivering mHealth education.
Proof-of-concept qualitative study using field study strategy; not an RCT.
Descriptive survey design; usability test, not an RCT.
Protocol publication, not results of an RCT.

RCT of HF patients. Intervention is collaborative care with home telemonitoring and self-management support, not specifically mHealth-delivered education. Multifaceted disease management, not a focused mHealth education trial.
Protocol/study design publication; not an RCT results paper.
RCT of HF patients; intervention: technology-enhanced practice with HeartCareII website (web-based home care resource, likely providing education). Comparator: usual home care. mHealth education.
RCT of HF patients, but intervention is face-to-face motivational interviewing sessions. Not mHealth-delivered education.
Participants have CVD or at risk, not specifically HF. Population does not meet HF diagnosis criterion.
RCT of HF patients. Intervention: mobile phone-assisted case management program, likely delivering education and support. mHealth intervention vs usual care.
RCT of HF patients; intervention is telehomecare (remote monitoring of clinical indices). Not specifically an mHealth education program; primarily monitoring and nurse communication.

RCT of older adults with HF; intervention is a telehealth system for data transmission. Focus on confidence and self-management, but not explicitly an educational intervention delivered via mHealth. Not clearly meeting education criterion.
RCT of HF patients post-discharge. Intervention: continued use of Health Buddy telehealth system (monitoring/communication device). Not an educational program; monitoring-focused.
RCT of stable HF patients. Intervention: internet-based synchronized face-to-face video group discussion/education sessions (mHealth education). Comparator: handout + Fitbit. Meets criteria.
Quasi-experimental design, convenience sample; not an RCT.
Development and feasibility study without a control group; not an RCT.
RCT (nurse-level randomization) but intervention is e-mail reminders to nurses, not mHealth education delivered to patients. No patient-facing mHealth education.
Feasibility study with convenience sample (n=10); no randomization, not an RCT.
Protocol/design paper, not results of an RCT.
Systematic literature review, not a primary RCT.
RCT of HF patients; intervention is telemonitoring medication adherence with telephonic support. Not an educational program; medication monitoring with reminders but no educational content delivery.
RCT but population includes both HF and COPD patients, not exclusively HF. Criteria require HF diagnosis; mixed population precludes inclusion.
RCT of HF patients; intervention is electronic pillbox and smartphone app for medication reminders. This is an adherence/reminder tool, not an educational intervention. No mHealth education content.
RCT of HF patients; intervention is remote medication monitoring system (MedSentry). No educational component; purely medication adherence monitoring device.
Not an RCT of an mHealth education intervention in HF; evaluation of integrated care service deployment across multiple chronic conditions.
Abstract describes a pilot trial of an exercise intervention for smoking reduction in disadvantaged smokers, not HF patients.
Internet-based telemedicine system for surveillance and communication, not an mHealth-delivered education program; no educational content described.
Web-based telemedicine system for monitoring and data reporting, not an education program.
Protocol of an RCT of a medication adherence telemonitoring device, not an educational intervention.
Overview of systematic reviews, not a primary RCT.
Economic model derived from meta-analysis, not a primary RCT.
Meta-analysis of RCTs on implantable device telemonitoring, not a primary RCT.
Both arms received an ICT-guided disease management system; not a comparison of mHealth education versus usual care. No isolated educational component.
Review of educational voice message studies, not an RCT.
Secondary analysis of a clinical trial, not a primary RCT of an education intervention.
Retrospective evaluation of a telephonic health coaching program; not an RCT and not a defined mHealth-delivered education program.
RCT in sedentary young adults without diagnosed HF; population does not meet inclusion criteria.
Mixed-methods pilot study with small sample, not a definitive RCT, and intervention was monitoring equipment, not an education program.
Qualitative study of telehealth experience, not an RCT.
Population recruited from general heart disease registries, not specifically HF; intervention was an online support group, not an education program.
Education delivered via Kodak Photo-CD and face-to-face, not an mHealth platform (no internet, app, SMS, or social media).
Interactive CD-ROM education, not an mHealth-delivered program.
Quasi-experimental design; intervention used video-tape/booklet and telephone, not an mHealth education program.
Single-arm pilot study (no control group), not an RCT.
Proof-of-concept study without a control group, not an RCT.
Pilot RCT of web-based CBT for depression, not an education program for HF self-care.
RCT of remote monitoring and fluid monitoring for patients with ICD/CRT devices, not an educational intervention.
Home telemonitoring of physiological parameters, not an education program.
Multidisciplinary disease management program, not an mHealth-delivered education program.
Protocol of an RCT of motivational interviewing, not an mHealth education intervention.
RCT of motivational interviewing, not an mHealth-delivered education program.
Cost-effectiveness modeling study, not an RCT.
Retrospective study of remote monitoring of ICDs, not an RCT of education.
RCT of e-mail reminders to nurses, not to HF patients; not a patient-level education intervention.
Telephone tele-monitoring intervention (voice calls) without explicit educational content; not an mHealth education program as defined.
Qualitative study of nurses' perceptions of telehealth, not an RCT.
RCT of remote patient monitoring with health coaching telephone calls (BEAT-HF); intervention is monitoring and coaching, not a structured mHealth-delivered education program.
Meta-analysis and narrative review of CHIT interventions, not a primary RCT.
Not an RCT; this is a review of monitoring devices. Does not describe an mHealth education intervention.

RCT, but the intervention is telephone‑based health coaching (voice calls). The protocol specifies mHealth‑delivered education (smartphone/tablet apps, web, SMS, social media). Telephony coaching is not clearly an mHealth education programme per the review’s definition.
RCT, telemonitoring plus telephone support, but the intervention focuses on monitoring vital signs, not on delivering education. Not an mHealth education programme.
RCT, but the intervention is remote patient monitoring via video‑based nursing visits, not an educational programme. Does not meet the education‑focused inclusion.
Qualitative study (focus groups), not an RCT.

RCT in HF patients. The intervention (“standard mHealth” and “mHealth+CarePartner”) consists of automated self‑care support calls and email summaries. This represents mHealth‑delivered education (self‑care support) sent to patients and caregivers via mobile‑mediated communication. Meets the review’s criteria.
Protocol paper – not a completed RCT with results.

RCT, but the E‑Coach intervention is an IVR‑based care transition programme (nurse‑coordinated, post‑discharge calls). The primary focus is care coordination, not an mHealth education programme. Educational content is not explicitly described.

RCT in HF patients. The intervention includes a web‑based electronic medical record with an educational guide and messaging. This is web‑based education, accessible via internet‑connected devices (including mobile), and meets the definition of mHealth‑delivered education.

RCT, but the population is not specifically patients with heart failure (targets multiple diseases). The intervention is risk‑tailored messages for primary prevention, not HF‑specific mHealth education.
The abstract does not describe a telehealth trial; it reports an observational analysis of HbA1c and mortality in T2DM and CHF. Not an RCT of a mHealth education intervention.
Qualitative focus group study, not an RCT.
Qualitative interview study, not an RCT.

RCT, but the intervention is a telemonitoring system (symptom/physiological monitoring and automated instructions). While delivered via mobile phone, it is primarily a monitoring/management tool, not an intentionally designed education programme. Does not meet the “education” requirement.
Study protocol, not a completed RCT.
Design and rationale paper, not a completed RCT with results.
RCT of a computer‑based educational program (likely CD‑ROM/desktop). Does not meet the mHealth requirement (smartphone/tablet/apps/web‑based; “computer‑based” is not specifically mobile).
Review/overview article, not an original RCT.
Study protocol, not a completed RCT.
Pilot trial of telemonitoring, not an education‑focused intervention. The technology is remote monitoring, not an mHealth education programme.
RCT, but the intervention is a DVD and booklet (physical media). Not mHealth‑delivered (no internet/mobile/SMS/web).
RCT using a handheld PDA for telemonitoring. The intervention is monitoring and communication, not an education programme.
Audit/survey, not an RCT.
Prospective study with retrospective matched controls, not a true RCT.
Retrospective study, not an RCT.
Retrospective chart review, not an RCT. (Abstract truncated, but design clearly not RCT.)
Feasibility study on healthy volunteers, not an RCT in HF patients.
Rationale/design paper; the abstract describes a different study (Bosnian war survivors), not a completed HF RCT.
Methodology paper (development of a taxonomy), not an RCT.
Registry‑based observational study, not an RCT.

RCT of a disease management programme that includes telephone‑based monitoring and education. However, the telephone component is voice‑based, not specifically mHealth (smartphone apps, SMS, web), thus not meeting the mHealth‑delivered education criterion.
Methodology paper (GRADE system), not an RCT.

RCT but the intervention is telephone‑based education (voice calls). Telephone alone is not included in the mHealth definition used in this review (requires internet, apps, SMS, social media, or web‑based programmes accessible on mobile devices).
Not a RCT; it is a narrative review describing the epidemiology and risk profile of HF, with no intervention or control group.
Not a RCT; it is a review article summarising literature on cognitive impairment detection in HF, not an interventional study.
Not a RCT; it is a review of epidemiology and outcomes in HFpEF, no intervention evaluated.
Not a RCT; it is a secondary cross-sectional analysis using regression models, without randomization or intervention.
RCT but the population is adults with type 2 diabetes, not heart failure. Therefore does not meet the population criterion.
Not a RCT; it is a prospective cohort study examining predictors of mortality, no intervention or randomization.
Not a RCT; it is a literature review summarising factors related to self-care, without any original intervention study.
RCT but the population is women with early-stage breast cancer, not heart failure. Does not meet the population criterion.
Not a primary RCT; it is an individual patient data meta-analysis of existing trials, not a direct comparison of a specific mHealth education intervention versus usual care.
Not a RCT; it is a meta-analysis of trial-level drug/device therapy effects on remodeling, not an individual trial of mHealth education.
Not a RCT; it is a literature review describing the measurement of patient satisfaction with telemedicine, no intervention compared.
Subgroup analysis of a RCT; the intervention is pharmacological (aliskiren/enalapril), not mHealth-delivered education. Does not meet intervention criterion.
Not a RCT; it is a scientific statement and classification system, not an experimental study.
Not a RCT; it is a systematic review of web-based interventions across chronic diseases, no primary data collection.
Not a RCT; it is a meta-analysis of previous studies, not a primary comparison of mHealth education.
Not a RCT; it is a systematic review, not an original interventional study.
Not a RCT; it is an observational cohort study assessing the association between numeracy and recidivism, with no intervention.
Not a RCT; it is a methodological paper developing a framework for behaviour change interventions, no patient-level trial.
Not a RCT; it is a meta-analysis, not a primary study.
Not a RCT; it is a before-after pre-post study without a control group. Does not meet RCT design criterion.
Not a RCT; it is a cross-sectional survey of providers, not an intervention study in patients.
Not a RCT; it is a systematic review/meta-analysis, and the targeted population is diabetes, not heart failure.
Not a RCT; it is a systematic review and network meta-analysis, not a primary trial.
Not a RCT; it is a commentary/discussion article on eHealth and community nursing, with no experimental design.
RCT but the population is young adults with depressive symptoms, not heart failure. Does not meet population criterion.
Not a RCT; it is a population-based cohort study examining trends, without an intervention.
Not a RCT; it is a multi-center observational study evaluating an online education program, with no randomization.
RCT but the population is lung transplant recipients, not heart failure. Does not meet population criterion.
Not a RCT; it is an observational cross-sectional study using regression analysis, without an intervention.
Not a RCT; it is a trial design paper for a drug comparison (sacubitril/valsartan vs enalapril), not mHealth education.
Not a RCT; it is a systematic review, not a primary interventional study.

RCT in HF patients, but the intervention is a printed ultrasound image with explanation, not mHealth-delivered education (internet, web, apps, SMS, social media). Does not meet intervention criterion.
Not a RCT; it is a developmental project with beta testing in 10 patients, lacking a control group or randomization.
Not a randomized controlled trial; described an IVRS provided to 60 inpatients without randomization.
Not an RCT; describes development and pilot evaluation; authors call for larger randomized trials.
